question.text: In the Hemant Ghai case, what was ordered regarding the open positions in derivatives contracts held by the restrained entities?

answer.text: They could close out/square up till 3 months from date of order
They had to be immediately liquidated
They were automatically cancelled by the exchange
They could be held until expiry

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 155), the order stated that any open position in derivatives contracts could be closed out or squared up till three months from the date of the order. The Trap: The other options invent alternative mechanics (immediate liquidation, automatic cancellation, holding until expiry) that the order did not impose. The source only specifies the three-month close-out/square-up window. Note: The three-month window is a specific feature of this restraint order and should be recalled directly from the source rather than reasoned from general principles.
